Thus the residual is O(ε) in the maximum norm but generally O(1), not O(ε), in BC1.

issues.failure_explanation: The implicit cubic equations need not have a unique solution for the allowed negative λ. On a constant demodulated periodic mode, with previous value zero and current value c, the next value y satisfies [K + λ|y|²/4 − iH]y = 2Kc, where K = ε²/τ² and H = ω/τ. Its squared-modulus equation is r[(K + λr/4)² + H²] = 4K²|c|². For λ < 0 and K² > 3H² this function is nonmonotone and suitable c give three positive roots. No bounded or continuation branch is specified. Linear stability alone cannot establish the nonlinear guarantee for these unspecified solutions.

issues.failure_explanation: At the carrier frequency θh = β, the displayed symbols give tildeγ = 1 and γ = −ωτ/ε². Hence tildeγ²/(1 + γ²) = 1/(1 + ω²τ²/ε⁴), which tends to 1 as τ/ε² tends to zero, fully consistently with the CFL condition. The eigenvectors coalesce and the companion matrix tends to the Jordan matrix with rows (2,−1) and (1,0). Arbitrary two-level initial errors can consequently be amplified by order ε²/τ; concentrating Fourier data near the carrier gives the same obstruction in the Wiener space. Crank–Nicolson has the identical carrier-mode degeneration. Thus no alternative invariant norm can have the claimed uniform equivalence on the stated pair space.
